direction: A bold Swiss utility website named VALVE. Saturated cobalt blue field, enormous white condensed sans-serif headline 'GOOD PLUMBING. NO DRAMA.' spans the top two thirds, small yellow rectangular 'Book a plumber' action, a crisp closeup chrome faucet photograph in a shallow panoramic strip along the bottom. Header white wordmark top left, minimal nav top right. Typography-led poster, absolutely no serif and no side-by-side text/photo hero.

An architectural electric company website named CURRENT. Near-black background with acid-yellow condensed typography, oversized 'POWER, PROPERLY.' across center. Wide twilight architectural photograph of a modern home with warm illuminated windows along bottom third. A narrow vertical cream navigation rail at left with rotated company wordmark and simple menu. Tiny yellow 'Get a quote' action upper right. Asymmetrical graphic, no serif, no white split hero.

A friendly modern heating and cooling website named EVERYDAY AIR. Warm cream background, coral orange oversized rounded lowercase title 'Comfort comes home.' centered at top. Centered photoreal white heat pump outdoor unit product cutout sits below the heading on pale apricot ground, small sage green 'Find your system' button. Three very clean short service columns along bottom. No people, no split layout, no serif. Stylish direct-to-consumer appliance brand feeling.

A confident roofing contractor website named RIDGELINE. Full-width dramatic overhead photo of a beautifully installed dark standing-seam roof, graphic solid vermilion RED left border 15% width with vertical wordmark, giant bold white sans 'BUILT FOR THE WEATHER.' placed low across the roof photograph. Across bottom a white horizontal strip 'Repairs / Replacement / New roofs' and red 'Request an estimate' button. Editorial construction campaign, no stock portrait, no serif, no conventional left-text-right-photo.

An art-directed garden landscape architecture website named FIELDWORK. Warm ivory page, enormous delicate dark olive serif wordmark FIELDWORK stretching across entire top quarter. Beneath, two unequal portrait photographs of an Okanagan courtyard garden with dry grasses and a stone pathway form an offset diptych, small italic 'A little more outside.' sits in whitespace between. Dark olive small rounded 'Start your garden' button under left image. Quiet botanical magazine with image mosaic and typographic masthead, not generic split hero.

An award-calibre architectural home builder website named FORMWOOD. Edge-to-edge photograph of an elegant cedar-and-concrete Okanagan house on a hillside at blue hour. Tiny white navigation discreet at top, huge transparent-feeling refined white sans wordmark FORMWOOD anchored across bottom edge over image. Only brief center-right text 'Considered homes. Beautifully built.' and simple underlined 'Explore the homes'. Cinematic architecture portfolio; no panels, no split layout, no stock people.

A playful highly functional appliance service website named FIXDAY. White background with oversized ultramarine chunky sans masthead 'LET’S GET IT WORKING.' across top, small orange 'Book a repair' rectangular button beneath. Bottom half is three neatly aligned appliance product photographs: silver refrigerator, white front-loading washer, stainless oven, each on flat yellow, light blue and coral backgrounds. Bold product catalogue grid, not a text-left/photo-right hero. Header logo simple black FIXDAY.

A beautifully restrained law firm website named ALDER LEGAL. Ivory and dark ink with a small rust accent. Centered formal serif typography 'Good counsel. Clear direction.' with generous whitespace in the upper two thirds. Discreet centered wordmark and fine hairline navigation at top, thin outlined 'Arrange a consultation' button beneath heading. A very shallow wide photograph of a wood-lined office/library at bottom edge. Typography-first calm legal journal, no split photo composition.

A sharply modern accounting website named TALLY. Kelly green full background with off-white clean geometric sans heading 'Know your numbers.' giant and centered across top half. Beneath it a structured three-column service area on cream: Tax, Bookkeeping, Advice, with large typographic 01 02 03. Small black 'Let’s talk' button top right. Thin black rules, rational Swiss grid, no people, NO serif, no generic photographic right-side panel. Subtle still life of a calculator and organized papers appears in one narrow bottom-right tile.

An editorial financial planning website named NORTHLINE. Midnight navy page with pale blue type. A narrow left navigation column with stacked small links and small cream wordmark; main content a huge expressive serif 'A plan for the life ahead.' centered, below a horizontal quiet black-and-white lakeshore landscape photograph. Small cream rectangular 'Start a conversation' action beside heading. Sophisticated magazine cover composition, ample dark negative space, no stock people, no charts or invented numbers.

A polished real estate property search website named LAKE & LAND. Full-width crisp sunlit image of a modern Okanagan lakefront home fills upper two thirds, enormous cream uppercase condensed sans wordmark LAKE & LAND spanning top, very small discrete nav. Along bottom quarter on white an actual simple listing search row: Location, Property type, Bedrooms and a dark green Search button, with 3 small listing thumbnails just visible below. Image-led property portal, no serif split hero.

A dynamic property management website named GOODKEEP. Warm orange background, oversized black grotesk 'GOOD PLACES. WELL KEPT.' stacked on left 60%, right 40% contains a staggered architectural photo mosaic of two apartment buildings, hard edged not rounded. Bottom a white full-width three-way navigation strip For owners / For residents / Find a rental. Clear black 'Talk to us' button upper right. Bold flat graphic branding, no serif, no muted cream lifestyle formula.

A crisp accessible family medical clinic website named WESTSIDE HEALTH. White with mint green and strong royal blue. Centered large bold sans text 'Care that starts with you.' at top, two prominent cobalt and outlined appointment actions centered below. Lower half is asymmetric three-panel strip: pale mint opening hours text, photoreal bright empty treatment room, pale blue New patients navigation. Precise clean Swiss clinical design, no serif, no stock people, no split hero.

A fresh distinctive dental studio website named LITTLE BLUE. Powder blue background, huge bright tomato red rounded sans lowercase masthead 'hello, healthy smile.' spans upper portion. Right below heading small red capsule 'Book a visit'. At bottom a playful architectural triptych of a real immaculate light blue dental interior: arched doorway, modern chair, brushed-metal dental instruments. White narrow top navigation, tiny black labels. Bold contemporary colour and friendly graphic design, no serif and no cream split hero.

A sports physiotherapy website named RANGE. Almost black background, giant compressed electric lime type 'MOVE LIKE YOU MEAN IT.' fills left two thirds. Right side is a close photographic crop of an empty training studio with strength rings, wooden plyo box and a kettlebell, framed by a hard diagonal cut. Lime full-width bottom strip with 'Physiotherapy / Recovery / Performance'. Small squared lime 'Book your assessment' action. Aggressive athletic editorial, no serif, no people, not a spa.

A luxury skin studio website named STILL SKIN. Pale dusty rose page with deep burgundy type. Ultra-large thin elegant serif word STILL across entire top half as masthead, below a narrow central portrait photograph of cream skincare bottles and a limestone basin, flanked by small carefully set treatment names. Centered burgundy small pill 'Find your treatment' at bottom. Fashion beauty editorial with huge typography and vertical still life, no people, no split hero.

A charismatic community charity website named COMMON TABLE. Warm saturated yellow background with huge bold black grotesk 'THERE’S ROOM FOR EVERYONE.' occupying upper center, tiny black navigation above. Bottom half a collage of three tactile photographs: a community garden bed, crates of fresh vegetables, a long empty wooden table in afternoon light. A red rectangular 'Give today' button overlaps whitespace at bottom right. Cultural institution graphic style, no sad stock portraits, no serif split.

An independent school website named CEDAR SCHOOL. A collegiate deep burgundy and cream design. Top cream band centered refined school wordmark with a small simple cedar emblem; beneath an editorial two-column photo spread of a sunlit brick campus and a library, a very large burgundy serif 'Curiosity belongs here.' positioned in a cream horizontal band between photos, and a small burgundy 'Visit our school' button lower left. Thoughtful school prospectus layout, no fake accreditation or statistics or children faces.

A cinematic boutique hotel website named WESTLAKE HOUSE. A single immersive photograph of a sunlit Okanagan lakefront terrace viewed through broad glass doors. Tiny centered white wordmark and minimal top nav. Very large elegant WHITE serif 'Stay a little longer.' centered over the darkest readable area. Across bottom a compact ivory booking bar Arrival / Departure / Guests / dark olive 'Check availability'. No side panels, no beige text-left/image-right, pure full-bleed photography.

An outdoor cabin rental website named OUT HERE. Burnt orange and cream bold playful slab-serif masthead OUT HERE at top, followed by a playful uneven three-photo collage: a warm A-frame cabin in pine trees largest center, a blue mountain lake left portrait, a fireside cabin reading nook right square. Small dark green handwritten-feeling line 'Your weekend, reclaimed.' below, dark green 'Find your cabin' pill at bottom. Contemporary travel magazine layout with bright graphic personality, no conventional split.

An exquisitely art-directed winery website named AFTERNOON. Deep plum solid background, enormous cream high-contrast serif AFTERNOON masthead across top. A single very photoreal olive-glass wine bottle with cream minimalist label centered tall in middle, flanked by a small editorial text 'Good wine. No hurry.' on left and thin line navigation 'Our wines / Visit / The vineyard' on right. Lower edge subtle panoramic strip of Okanagan vines at sunset. Wine-as-product poster, no giant split landscape hero.

A design-led restaurant website named SALT & STEM. Rich burgundy and pale butter-yellow palette. Enormous condensed sans SALT & STEM wordmark filling top third. Lower center a large beautiful circular overhead photograph of a plated seasonal dish on burgundy background, slim menu navigation down left, right side small stacked white 'Dinner. Drinks. Good company.' and a butter-yellow squared 'Book a table' action. Restaurant menu poster composition, no serif, no split lifestyle image.

A vibrant independent design store ecommerce website named OBJECTS. Electric blue and white Swiss style. Huge blue grotesk wordmark OBJECTS spans top quarter on white. Under thin category nav, a very clean three-column product catalogue: sculptural terracotta vase on pale pink, cobalt table lamp on butter yellow, wooden stool on pale blue. Each has small plain product name and a simple shop link, no fake prices. A narrow blue strip says 'Good things, for everyday.' No generic single hero photo or serif split.

A contemporary automotive dealer website named OPEN ROAD. Graphite grey background, oversized angular white sans OPEN ROAD masthead across top with small red accent. A realistic silver SUV in clean side profile occupies the entire central width on a simple pale grey seamless ground, dramatic but believable automotive photography. Bottom a black horizontal inventory search bar Make / Model / Budget / a vivid red 'Find your next car' button. Bold engineering-led design, no people, no serif, no split hero.
